'''Jeremy John Baumberg''', {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|sep=,|FRS|FInstP}} (born 14 March 1967) is a British physicist who is [[professor]] of [[nanoscience]] in the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], a [[fellow]] of [[Jesus College, Cambridge]], and director of the [[Nanophotonics|NanoPhotonics]] Centre.{{cn|date=November 2023}}

==Education==
Baumberg was born on 14 March 1967. He was educated at the [[University of Cambridge]], where he was an undergraduate student of [[Jesus College, Cambridge]], and awarded a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in [[Natural Sciences (Cambridge)|natural sciences]] in 1988.{{cn|date=November 2023}} He moved to the [[University of Oxford]], where he was awarded a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in 1993. During his postgraduate study he was a student of [[Jesus College, Oxford]], and supervised by John Francis Ryan, where his doctoral research investigated [[nonlinear optics]] in [[semiconductor]]s.{{cn|date=November 2023}}

==Career and research==
Following his PhD, Baumberg was a visiting [[IBM]] [[Research fellow]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara|University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB)]] from 1994 to 1995.{{cn|date=November 2023}} He returned to the UK to work in the [[Hitachi]] Cambridge Lab<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hit.phy.cam.ac.uk/|website=hit.phy.cam.ac.uk|title=Hitachi Cambridge Laboratory|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808221744/http://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/obituaries/prof-simon-baumberg-1-2464752|archive-date=2017-08-08}}</ref> from 1995 to 1998 before being appointed professor of nano-scale physics at the [[University of Southampton]]{{cn|date=November 2023}} from 1998 to 2007 where he co-founded Mesophotonics Limited, a Southampton [[University spin-off]] company.{{cn|date=November 2023}}

Baumberg's research is in [[nanotechnology]],<ref name=frs/> including [[nanophotonics]], [[plasmon]]ics, [[metamaterial]]s and [[Optical microcavity|optical microcavities]]. He is interested in the development of nanostructured optical materials that undergo unusual interactions with [[light]], and his research has various commercial applications.<ref name=ft>{{cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/1af0efea-1045-11e6-bb40-c30e3bfcf63b|publisher=[[Financial Times]]|location=London|website=ft.com|title=Quantum technologies: Scientists build world's tiniest engine|first=Clive|last=Cookson|year=2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808032952/https://www.ft.com/content/1af0efea-1045-11e6-bb40-c30e3bfcf63b|archive-date=2017-08-08}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/2016/05/04/british-scientists-create-worlds-tiniest-engine---a-million-time/|website=telegraph.co.uk|publisher=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|title=British scientists create world's tiniest engine - a million times smaller than an ant|first=Adam|last=Boult|year=2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809185841/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/2016/05/04/british-scientists-create-worlds-tiniest-engine---a-million-time/|archive-date=2017-08-09}}</ref> His early work led to the development of a number of pioneering experimental techniques.<ref name=frs/> 

Baumberg appeared in the documentary ''The Secret Life of Materials'' in 2015 and a ''[[Horizon (UK TV series)|Horizon]]'' documentary about [[Schön scandal]] first broadcast in 2004.<ref name=imdb>{{IMDb name|id=1580910}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sci/tech/3459769.stm|website=news.bbc.co.uk|publisher=[[BBC]]|first=Nick|last=Green|year=2004|title=Nano-scientist's dark secret|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070120182214/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sci/tech/3459769.stm|archive-date=2007-01-20}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
Baumberg has received several awards for his research including the [[Mullard Award]] in 2004 and [[Rumford Medal]] in 2014, both from the [[Royal Society]].<ref name=frs/> The [[Institute of Physics|Institute of Physics (IOP)]] awarded Baumberg with the Silver [[Young Medal and Prize]] in 2013<ref name=young>{{cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/silver/young/medallists/page_38619.html|title=Young Medal recipients|website=iop.org|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808221744/http://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/obituaries/prof-simon-baumberg-1-2464752|archive-date=2017-08-08}}</ref> and the Gold [[Faraday Medal and Prize]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/faraday/medallists/page_38448.html|title=Faraday medal recipients|website=iop.org|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808221744/http://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/obituaries/prof-simon-baumberg-1-2464752|archive-date=2017-08-08}}</ref> Baumberg was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2011|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2011]].<ref name=frs>{{cite web|website=royalsociety.org|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|author=Anon|year=2011|title=Professor Jeremy Baumberg FRS|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/jeremy-baumberg-11056/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628120846/https://royalsociety.org/people/jeremy-baumberg-11056/|archive-date=2017-06-28}}</ref>

==Publications==

==Personal life==
Baumberg is the son of the late Simon Baumberg [[Order of the British Empire|OBE]],<ref name=whowaswho>{{Who's Who | title=BAUMBERG, Prof. Simon | id = U6830 | year = 2017 | edition = online |location=Oxford|type=was|author=Anon|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U6830}}</ref> a [[microbiologist]] and who served as Professor of [[bacterial genetics]]  at the [[University of Leeds]] from 1966 to 2005.<ref name=whowaswho/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2007/jul/06/obituaries.mainsection|website=[[The Guardian]]|title=Simon Baumberg Obituary|first=Colin|last=Harwood|year=2007|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170804215048/https://www.theguardian.com/news/2007/jul/06/obituaries.mainsection|archive-date=2017-08-04}}</ref><ref name=yorks>{{cite news|url=http://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/obituaries/prof-simon-baumberg-1-2464752|newspaper=[[The Yorkshire Post]]|title=Prof Simon Baumberg Obituary: Outstanding microbiologist|author=Anon|year=2007|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808221744/http://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/news/obituaries/prof-simon-baumberg-1-2464752|archive-date=2017-08-08}}</ref>
